Adjust the display range

Source: R/adjust-exposure.R
adjust_exposure.Rd

Sets how image intensities map to brightness: intensities at or below min are shown black, at or above max in full colour. Like in ImageJ, this is a display property and does not change the image data.

Usage

adjust_exposure(montage, min = "p0.1", max = "p99.9", ..., .by = channel)

Arguments

montage

A tidymontage() object.

min, max

Lower and upper end of the display range: a percentile of the pixel intensities as a string such as "p0.1" or "p99.9", or an intensity value such as 0 or 4000.

...

Per-channel exceptions as name-value pairs, for example DAPI = c(0, 2000) or DAPI = c("p1", "p99").

.by

Columns that define which images share a display range, as a bare name or c() of names. Default: channel.

Value

The montage with the exposure step added.

Details

By default, display ranges are linked per channel: all images of one channel share the same range, computed from all of them together, so that brightness can be compared across conditions. This is also what happens without calling adjust_exposure(). To unlink on purpose, group more finely, for example .by = c(channel, condition).

A data column display_min and/or display_max in the images tibble overrides the range for single images.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
montage |> adjust_exposure(min = "p0.1", max = "p99.9")
montage |> adjust_exposure(DAPI = c(0, 3000))
} # }
